title: The Princess and the Pea
blurb: A queen hides one pea under twenty mattresses to test a girl.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… there was a Prince who wanted to marry a princess. [firmly] But she had to be a REAL princess. Not almost. Not nearly. A real one.

[thoughtful] So he travelled all over the world to find one. [sad] And he came home again with nobody at all.

[curious] Oh, there were princesses enough. But there was always something not quite right about them, and he could never be sure.

[softly] So the Prince sat at home, and he was very sad, because he did so want a real princess.

[worried] Then one evening, a terrible storm came. [loudly] Lightning cracked across the sky. Thunder rolled over the rooftops. The rain came down in sheets, and the wind pulled at the shutters.

[surprised] And in the middle of it all… somebody knocked at the city gate.

[calmly] The old King himself went down to open it.

[surprised] And there, standing outside in the storm, was a girl. [sad] Oh, but what a state she was in. The water ran out of her hair and down her clothes. It ran in at the toes of her shoes and out again at the heels. She was soaked right through.

[firmly] “I am a real princess,” she said.

[amused] Well. [thoughtful] The old Queen looked at her, dripping on the doorstep, and said nothing at all.

[mischievously] But she thought a great deal.

[whispers] And she went quietly up to the spare bedroom, and she took every single thing off the bed, right down to the wooden boards. [short pause] And on the boards, she laid one small green pea.

[excited] Then she called for mattresses. [amused] Twenty mattresses were carried up the stairs and piled on top of that pea. And on top of the twenty mattresses, twenty thick feather beds.

[playfully] The pile went nearly to the ceiling. The girl had to climb a ladder to get into bed at all.

[softly] “Sleep well,” said the Queen. [mischievously] And she went away and shut the door.

[curious] In the morning, they asked her how she had slept.

[annoyed] “Oh, dreadfully,” said the girl. “I hardly closed my eyes the whole night. [worried] There was something HARD in that bed. I lay on something so hard that I am black and blue all over. [sad] It was quite, quite dreadful.”

[excited] And then they knew. [warmly] Nobody but a real princess could feel one small pea through twenty mattresses and twenty feather beds.

[happy] So the Prince married her, and he was very glad, because now he was quite sure.

[amused] And the pea? The pea was put in a museum, where it may still be seen to this day — [whispers] unless somebody has taken it.
